title: Mandatory electronic conveyancing (New South Wales)
summary: NSW required standalone transfers, standalone caveats, and mortgages and discharges (including refinances) to be lodged electronically from 1 July 2018, under Version 4 of the Registrar General's Conveyancing Rules (in force from 15 May 2018), and all mainstream land dealings from 1 July 2019.

instruments.title: Registrar General's requirements under the Electronic Conveyancing National Law (NSW)
instruments.provisions: electronic lodgment mandates (instrument versions not checked)

commenced.what: Electronic lodgment required for standalone transfers, standalone caveats, and mortgages and discharges (Conveyancing Rules v4)
Electronic lodgment required for all mainstream dealings

direction_rationale: Mandatory electronic lodgment cuts settlement costs and time for conveyancers and lenders, but in practice it entrenched one electronic lodgment network (PEXA), because interoperability between networks never went live.
comparison: Staggered mandates 2018-2023; the ACT, Tasmania and the NT have no mandate (never treated)
confounders: housing market swings and interest rate changes

verified.notes: Corrected in the fact-check of 6 Nov 2026: the first mandate is 1 July 2018, not 1 May 2018. Registrar General, 'Revised Conveyancing Rules' (13 Apr 2018): Version 4 replaces Version 3 on 15 May 2018 and makes standalone transfers, standalone caveats, and mortgages and discharges mandatory for electronic lodgment from 1 July 2018. 1 July 2019: Registrar General, NSW eConveyancing news (June 2019): 'mandatory for you to lodge all mainstream dealings electronically from 1 July 2019'.

review.notes: Drafted by AI-assisted desk research on 18 October 2026 (legislation gap scan, docs/legislation_gap_scan.md) from the sources cited. Not yet checked: verify dates, industries and the direction hypothesis before use.

assessment.summary: Requires property transfers and mortgages to be lodged electronically. Settlement is faster and cheaper, but with no working interoperability between networks the mandate entrenched a single lodgement network.

marks.reason: Electronic lodgement and settlement cut paperwork, settlement time and errors.
Moves conveyancing onto a digital platform.
Without interoperability, mandatory electronic lodgement entrenched one network (PEXA) as a near-monopoly supplier.

assessment.confidence_note: The archived econometric evaluation found no detectable effect on business entry in legal services (grade Weak).
